evidence.summary: Exhaustive sweep of all 63,488 finite FP16 values: 16,664 nonzero inputs exceed the 1e-6 relative tolerance; max relative error is 1.5754e-6 (e.g. x=27.359375 gives 3.0132563 vs target 3.0132516). Signed zeros map exactly to zero, but the single Newton step does not achieve the contract's accuracy across the domain.

rationale: Only one Newton correction step is applied to a rough polynomial seed, which may leave relative error above 1e-6 for some mantissas; the FP16 domain is finite and small enough to test exhaustively.

scope_evidence.summary: Every finite FP16 value is legal, including subnormals and ±65504; every nonzero input must satisfy abs(actual - cbrt(x)) <= 1e-6*abs(cbrt(x)), and zero inputs must map to zero with zero absolute tolerance.

scope_rationale: Contract requires relative tolerance 1e-6 (and exact zero for zero inputs) over every finite FP16 value; any violation in that set is a contract breach.
statement: The kernel's one-Newton-step approximation fails to meet the 1e-6 relative tolerance on some finite FP16 input (or mishandles zero/subnormal/endpoint values).
